questions.heading: Start From the Requirements, and Make Each One a Yes-or-No Test
questions.stem: A candidate solver finishes the benchmark set quickest but rounds continuous variables and reports success. The service's model has a continuous carry-over variable. Where does that candidate belong in the memo?

options.text: As the default, since its speed outweighs one variable's rounding
options.says: A rounded continuous variable gives a wrong plan with no error; no speed makes up for that.

options.text: As the fallback, since it still solved every benchmark instance
options.says: The benchmark model has no continuous variable, so solving it says nothing about the carry-over model.

options.text: In the evidence, since its rounding is a measured cost to weigh
options.says: A requirement is a yes-or-no test applied before evidence; CP-SAT is ruled out at step 2, not weighed at step 3.

options.text: Out at the requirements, since its rounding fails a hard test
options.says: Right: the memo rules CP-SAT out on exact_continuous before reading any benchmark number.

questions.heading: The Evidence Is What the Harness Can Repeat, and Wall Time Enters Only as a Masked Check
questions.stem: A harness reports solver P with a worst seed spread of 1.3 and an LP-iteration mean of 9,000, and solver Q with 3.0 and 2,000. Which statement may the memo make?

options.text: Q does under a quarter of P's work across the seeds, since its mean is lower
options.says: Counts of different solvers are different units; they compare runs of one solver only.

options.text: P's effort depends less on the seed, since spreads are ratios with no unit
options.says: Right: the seed spread is unit-free, so it is the one work figure the memo compares across solvers.

options.text: Q is the faster solver for these seeds, since its mean count is lower
options.says: Speed across solvers needs wall time on every repetition by a stated factor; counts cannot show it.

options.text: P is the faster solver for these seeds, since its spread is lower
options.says: A low spread means predictable effort, not short runs; it says nothing about seconds.

questions.heading: Name a Default, a Fallback, and What Would Change the Decision
questions.stem: At the review, someone asks why the team does not simply buy Gurobi. Following this lesson's memo, what is the answer?

options.text: Never, since a commercial solver cannot be licensed inside a container
options.says: It can, through WLS or a token server; the memo prices that route instead of ruling it out forever.

options.text: Yes, since the public benchmarks show it ahead of every open solver
options.says: Gurobi withdrew from Mittelmann's benchmarks in August 2024, so no current public table shows that.

options.text: Not now, and here are the measurable conditions that would reopen it
options.says: Right: section 5 names a large solve missing its window, a network route to a license service, and an upgrade.

options.text: Not now, since the harness measured it slower than the open solvers
options.says: Gurobi was never run in the harness; it was ruled out by requirements, not by a measurement.
